item.title: Global experts hail China's Pinglu Canal, praise remarkable engineering, ecological achievements
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Global experts hail China's Pinglu Canal, praise remarkable engineering, ecological achievements A vessel sails along the Pinglu Canal near the Madao hub. Photo: Courtesy of Pinglu Canal Group The newly opened Pinglu Canal in South China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region has become a focal point of discussion for industry experts from home and abroad at the ongoing World Canals Conference 2026 (WCC) in Guilin, Guangxi, as many hailed the canal's economic value, engineering feats and ecological contribution. The conference runs from Monday to Friday in Guilin. Notably, this year's event closely follows the recent opening of the Pinglu Canal, which is also located in the autonomous region in South China. The 134.2-kilometer Pinglu Canal is the first canal planned and coordinated at the national level since 1949 to connect a river to the sea, and it opens up the shortest, most economical, and most convenient sea outlet for southwestern China. It is a backbone project of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor that connects with the China-proposed Belt and Road Initiative and marks a major addition to the nation's river network. The project has set four world records among comparable canals: the highest navigation capacity, the fastest ship-lock transit speed, the highest lift for a water-saving ship lock, and the largest water-saving ship lock on an inland waterway. As hundreds of canal experts from home and abroad gathered in Guilin, the Pinglu Canal's engineering achievements as well as other features such as ecological protection, were constantly acknowledged by participants in the event. "There is something quite remarkable about witnessing the beginning of an entirely new canal corridor," Sharon Leighton, president of Inland Waterways International, said at the opening ceremony of the event on Tuesday. "The Pinglu Canal introduces a new chapter in the long story of populations using waterways to connect and create opportunity." "Of everything I know, this is remarkable and leading," Leighton told the Global Times on Monday, commenting on the canal's engineering achievements in solving technical difficulties. Tomas Kolark, a canal expert from the Czech Republic, told the Global Times that the Pinglu Canal is very impressive in terms of engineering and water management. "I was watching closely the preparations and mainly the construction of the canal, and it was very interesting to see it now with my own eyes," Kolark said. "Another interesting approach of the canal was, for example, it is maybe one of the world's first bridges for wildlife crossings." As a project built with protecting the environment and ecology in mind, the Pinglu Canal has built fish passages, animal bridges and bird corridors, reflecting a deliberate effort to harmonize infrastructure with nature, the Global Times learned from Pinglu Canal Group, the builder of the canal. "It was interesting to see that 98 percent of the material excavated from the canal's construction was used for construction purposes. In all, it's very interesting to see how the canal was planned and built, and we could see today how it's used," said Kolark. Eddie Lee, a participant in the event, told the Global Times that she learned through visits to some of the hubs along the Pinglu Canal, where she saw how engineers tackled the difficulties in managing the high-water lift. She also understood the special technology used on the ship lock's gates to ensure smooth opening and closing while withstanding the high pressure. "It's interesting to know that Chinese engineers have worked with academia and top technology universities to tackle the issues," Lee said. "I understand that it will be very important for the economy in Guangxi, in [Southwest China's] Guizhou Province, and in [Southwest China's] Yunnan Province. I have traveled a lot in China, seeing that some southern parts have not developed as fast as northern or eastern parts. I think the Pinglu Canal will make a big difference." For its achievement, the Pinglu Canal Project was awarded the Green Design International Award by the World Green Design Organization on Tuesday, according to the Beijing-based stdaily.com. item.title: China's commerce minister meets Danone CEO, discusses deeper cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
China's commerce minister meets Danone CEO, discusses deeper cooperation BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao met with Antoine de Saint-Affrique, chief executive officer of Danone, a leading global food and beverage company, on Monday. The two sides exchanged views on Danone's development in China and on China-EU and China-France economic and trade relations, the commerce ministry said in a press release on Tuesday. Noting that China is firmly expanding high-level opening up, Wang said that the Chinese consumer market continues to grow, and its consumption structure keeps upgrading, providing broad space for foreign-invested enterprises to develop in the country. Wang welcomed Danone to expand investment, innovation and research and development in China, and to provide more quality products and services to both the Chinese and international markets. Wang added that the recent meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism reached a series of outcomes and consensus, which has stabilized business expectations. He expressed the hope that Danone will play a positive role in advancing China-EU and China-France economic and trade relations. For his part, de Saint-Affrique said Danone is optimistic about the prospects of the Chinese market, and will continue to increase investment in China and strengthen the research and development of new products. He added that the company is willing to contribute to EU-China and France-China economic and trade cooperation. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi meets Togo's president of Council of Ministers, elevating bilateral ties to community with shared future for new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Xi meets Togo's president of Council of Ministers, elevating bilateral ties to community with shared future for new era Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé in Beijing on Tuesday, during which the two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Togo community with a shared future for the new era. Xi pointed out that the traditional China-Togo friendship was personally forged by leaders of an older generation of both countries, enjoying a solid foundation and growing ever stronger with the passage of time. China and Togo share aligned visions for friendly cooperation and enjoy broad prospects ahead, Xi said. Xi called on the two sides to further enhance exchanges at all levels between the two parties and the two countries, deepen the sharing of experiences in governance, and firmly support each other on issues concerning core interests and major concerns. China welcomes Togo to effectively utilize measures such as China's zero-tariff policy and the "green channel" for products exported to China, further enhance its role as a regional hub for trade and logistics, and facilitate the entry of more distinctive local and regional products into the Chinese market, Xi added. Xi noted that China appreciates Togo's efforts to expand the cross-border use of the RMB and is willing to strengthen cooperation with Togo in new energy, digital intelligence and other fields to support Togo's industrialization process. Noting that China and Togo share similar positions on international and regional affairs, Xi also called on the two sides to enhance multilateral coordination. Xi put forward four principles for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa. First, adhering to the principle of "Africa-led." The African people are the true masters of Africa and should play a central role in regional affairs, Xi said. Second, upholding fairness and justice. All participating parties should abide by the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned, he noted. Third, promoting ceasing hostilities for peace. Wars and unilateral sanctions cannot fundamentally resolve conflicts between countries. It is imperative to uphold mutual respect, conduct extensive consultations, seek common ground while shelving differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation. Fourth, addressing both symptoms and root causes. Efforts should focus on immediate security while planning for long-term development, Xi said. Faure, who is on an official visit to China, said that during his visit, he personally witnessed the remarkable achievements of Chinese modernization and the extensive promotion of fine traditional Chinese culture under the leadership of President Xi, and gained a deeper understanding of China's governance philosophy and the key to success. Noting that next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, he said Togo is willing to enhance mutual trust with China, strengthen dialogue and communication, deepen enduring and mutually beneficial cooperation to jointly build a Togo-China community with a shared future for the new era, and better benefit the two peoples. The Togolese side fully agrees with the important principles proposed by President Xi for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa, Faure said. He expressed Togolese appreciation for China on its significant role in maintaining world peace and stability and jointly addressing global challenges, as well as the willingness to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China, jointly uphold multilateralism, and safeguard the interests of developing countries. item.title: China, Botswana establish comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
China, Botswana establish comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan hold a welcome ceremony for Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko and his wife Kaone Boko in the Northern Hall of the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. Xi held talks with Boko, who is on a state visit to China, after the welcome ceremony in Beijing on Tuesday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- During their talks in Beijing on Tuesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Noting that this year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China and the 60th anniversary of Botswana's independence, Xi said the two countries' ruling parties should strengthen cooperation and deepen exchanges on governance experience. China supports Botswana in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said. He called on both sides to further improve the framework for economic and trade cooperation, and tap into new opportunities created by China's zero-tariff policy for African countries that have diplomatic ties with China. China is ready to strengthen cooperation with Botswana in the digital economy, agriculture, animal husbandry and other sectors, and to carry out the smart education project, Xi added. On promoting China-Botswana and China-Africa mining cooperation, Xi said Africa's resources belong to Africa, and this is the premise for cooperation. China is willing to share its own experience and help African countries formulate mining development plans tailored to their national conditions, and China will encourage Chinese enterprises to transfer green technologies suited to African conditions, Xi said. He said China will continue to promote China-Africa mining cooperation to move up the value chain and explore affordable, sustainable and innovative financing models. Noting that Africa's resources should not become a tool for geopolitical rivalry, Xi said China welcomes all parties' genuine contributions to Africa's development and stands ready to work with Africa to create a more enabling environment for investment and business operations. China has lifted all its poor population out of poverty and forged a successful development path with Chinese characteristics, from which Botswana has much to learn, Boko noted. He said that Botswana highly values its ties with China, and will firmly adhere to the one-China principle and oppose any separatist moves toward "Taiwan independence" and any external interference in China's internal affairs. Botswana is willing to strengthen development strategy alignment with China and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in Botswana, said Boko. He added that the country stands ready to maintain close coordination and cooperation with China, uphold multilateralism, strengthen the solidarity of developing countries, promote Africa-China solidarity and cooperation, and make the global governance system more inclusive and representative. After their talks, the two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering such areas as implementing the Global Security Initiative, Belt and Road cooperation, green minerals, health, and human resources. During Boko's state visit to China, the two sides issued a joint statement on establishing a China-Botswana comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan held a welcome ceremony for Boko and his wife Kaone Boko in the Great Hall of the People. Xi and Peng also held a welcome banquet for them in the evening. item.title: Doolittle Raiders kin honor Sino-U.S. wartime friendship 84 years on
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Doolittle Raiders kin honor Sino-U.S. wartime friendship 84 years on NANCHANG, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Eighty-four years after the first U.S. air strike on the Japanese home islands during World War II, family members of some of the airmen traveled across the Pacific to retrace mountain paths where Chinese peasants risked torture and death to shelter downed American flyers, and to honor a friendship forged in wartime. This file photo taken in 1942 shows Guan Dongxiang (C) standing behind an American pilot, who participated in the Doolittle Raid. (Xinhua) In Yangcun Village, Shangrao City of east China's Jiangxi Province, Thomas Macia first met 94-year-old Guan Dongxiang, who was still a short-haired little girl gaping behind an American pilot, Jack Sims, copilot of the Doolittle Raid's Crew No. 14, in a black-and-white photo. James Macia, Thomas Macia's father, served as navigator and bombardier in the same aircrew. When he was nine, Thomas first saw the photo in his father's album. In the spring of 1942, Guan's father, Guan Wenqing, and fellow villagers helped rescue Sims in nearby Miliang'ao Village. Days later, the pilot returned with a camera and took the photo. "There she is!" Thomas Macia exclaimed at the first sight of the silver-haired Chinese woman on Sunday, along with five others from the Children of the Doolittle Raiders. "I knew she existed. I had not met her before. The greatest thing is that she is a direct connection to 1942." Thomas Macia (L), son of James Macia, holds the hand of Guan Dongxiang in Shangrao, east China's Jiangxi Province, Oct. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhou Mi) RETRACING WARTIME RESCUE In April 1942, 16 U.S. bombers led by Lieutenant Colonel James Doolittle took off from the USS Hornet aircraft carrier to bomb Japan, in retaliation for the attack on Pearl Harbor. After the operation, 15 planes heading for a designated airport in east China's Zhejiang Province ran out of fuel and crashed in various localities, including Jiangxi. Chinese villagers risked their lives to rescue the parachuting airmen behind enemy lines and helped them evacuate to safety. Of the 75 airmen whose aircraft came down, 64 were brought to safety. The rescue came at a tremendous cost. Many locals were suspected of sheltering the Americans, and some were tortured or even killed by Japanese invading soldiers. After the raid, Japan launched a three-month campaign in May 1942 to destroy air bases, airports and other infrastructure in Zhejiang and Jiangxi, to prevent them from being used by Chinese or U.S. air forces. The invading Japanese troops also waged biological warfare by spreading cholera, plague and other diseases, resulting in massive civilian deaths. Descendants of the rescued Doolittle Raid participants view a historical exhibition in Shangrao, east China's Jiangxi Province, Oct. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhou Mi) During a visit to Miliang'ao Village, Thomas recounted how his father landed in the mountains: "He could see off the top of the mountain, and he was hugging a small pine tree for the night to keep from sliding down." A visit to Dapai Mountain helped Thomas better understand his father's ordeal. "For me, to walk a little way up the hill ... I could imagine what my father did to know more exact information and the sense of what it looked like more than 80 years ago," he said. Gusty winds swept away his father's backpack and supplies as he parachuted down. Local villagers brought him eggs, honey and other food, and lit fires to dry his clothes. He was later escorted to the township government office, where he was reunited with other crew members. Thomas's father once pointed to a spot on a map and told his son that his life was saved by Chinese villagers, officials and soldiers, whom he remembered to his last breath. Thomas Macia donates a piece of fabric from the parachute of his father, James Macia, in Shangrao, east China's Jiangxi Province, Oct. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhou Mi) REDISCOVERING SHARED MEMORY Unable to return to China in his lifetime, James Macia kept the photograph with care. His son later made it his own mission to find the descendants of those lifesavers in person. In 2018, Thomas traveled to China for the first time and met Luo Shiping, a researcher with the Shangrao Anti-Japanese War Culture Research Association. The two have exchanged about 1,000 emails ever since. Over the years, Thomas combed through U.S. archives and provided clues, while Luo visited all crash sites and parachute landing areas across Shangrao, interviewed villagers and compiled investigation reports. After the war, Doolittle Raiders and their descendants established organizations such as the Children of the Doolittle Raiders. They hold annual commemorations, seminars and photo exhibitions to honor the Chinese who took part in the rescue. Researchers in Shangrao have continued to collect scattered documents and oral testimonies, working with their American counterparts to preserve this transnational memory. Their work has helped bring the heroic story to a wider audience. An exhibition on the rescue at Shangrao Museum has attracted almost 300,000 visitors since its opening in August 2025, according to museum curator Jiang Jinmin. On Saturday, the visiting Children of the Doolittle Raiders group toured the exhibition. Tom Johnson, son-in-law of Crew No. 14 pilot John Hilger, stopped now and then to snap photos of the displays. "Shangrao established and created this wonderful place of memory. It makes us know what they (Doolittle Raiders) accomplished," Johnson said. The delegation donated historical memorabilia to the museum, including fabric from the parachute used by James Macia, historical photos and relevant news clippings. Descendants of the rescued Doolittle Raid participants plant a tree of friendship with local people in Shangrao, east China's Jiangxi Province, Oct. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhou Mi) ENDURING FRIENDSHIP On Saturday, the delegation also visited a 140-year-old residence in Fujia Village, where five members of Crew No. 14 posed for a group photo during the war. Tears welled up in Thomas's eyes as he entered the house. He had seen the airmen's group photo as a child. "I've been told for years that this (house) was destroyed. But here it is," he said. Fu Yuntuo, still a boy and a descendant of the house's former owner, approached Thomas and told him that his family elders had often told him stories about the American airmen who once stayed in the house. Friendship is the greatest bond in the world, Fu said. For Thomas, his connection with Shangrao extends beyond historical research. Whenever floods, earthquakes or other disasters strike southern China, including Jiangxi, he contacts Luo to ask whether the area has been affected. "The Doolittle Raid embodies Chinese and American elders fighting side by side against fascism through adversity for WWII victory," Luo said. "I will work with Thomas to pass the stories on to younger generations of both nations." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a national meeting on health in Beijing, capital of China. The meeting was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to firmly follow a path with Chinese characteristics in developing the country's health programs, to secure decisive progress in the Healthy China Initiative over the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a national meeting on health held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Xi stressed that people's health is a key benchmark of a nation's prosperity and strength. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the Party has made a major decision to launch the Healthy China Initiative, promoting the establishment of the world's largest systems of medical services, traditional medicine, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security, said Xi, noting that the country has achieved historic accomplishments and made all-round progress in healthcare. In 2025, China's average life expectancy rose to 79.25 years, while its major health indicators remained at the leading position among upper-middle-income countries and countries with a population exceeding 100 million. Xi said the goal is to build a Healthy China, where health services are ensured in a balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient manner. Xi stressed that people's health should be factored into all policies and reflected in every aspect of work. Prevention, he said, is the most cost-effective and efficient approach to protecting public health. He called for greater emphasis on foundational health work, addressing risks at their source, and encouraging the public to adopt a sound understanding of health and take an active role in managing their own well-being. He also called for a stronger disease prevention and control system to guard against large-scale outbreaks. Xi underscored the need to optimize the functions and structural layout of medical institutions so that people can access medical care close to home and receive effective treatment. China has supported the development of 125 regional medical centers in areas where high-quality medical resources are relatively scarce. Notably, more than 90 percent of residents can access nearby medical and healthcare services within 15 minutes, while primary-level medical institutions account for over 50 percent of all medical visits nationwide. He also urged efforts to improve mechanisms for the preservation and innovative development of traditional Chinese medicine, strengthen basic research and original innovation in the health sector, and enhance the patient experience. Xi stressed that coordinating the development and regulation of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals should be a key priority in reforming China's medical and healthcare systems. He also called for efforts to train and develop a sufficient number of highly qualified medical professionals. Efforts will also be made to actively promote the building of a global community of health for all, work with other countries to address major challenges in the health sector, and continuously improve the health and well-being of people around the world, he said. Other Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the event. In his concluding remarks, Li Qiang said Xi's important speech provided guidance for advancing China's health sector. Li called for better coordination between improvements in public health and economic and social development, and urged deeper reform, innovation, opening up and cooperation, stronger prevention and control of major diseases, further development of a tiered diagnosis and treatment system, and greater use of science and technology to improve health services.
